Size is where we stop, and Iowa State University Extension tells homeowners the same thing: trimming large trees should be left to trained arborists.

blocks.title: Trees do not heal. **They grow over it.**
body: A tree does not heal a wound the way skin does. It walls the cut off and slowly grows over it. Iowa State University Extension calls this compartmentalization, and a clean cut in the right spot is what lets it happen. So where the saw goes matters.

The right cut goes back to a side branch or the trunk, just outside the raised collar where the branch starts, because a cut there closes best. And light beats heavy. Extension limits run from a quarter of the live foliage on maples (Minnesota) to a third of the crown on a young tree (Wisconsin), and an established tree usually needs much less.
checks: Heavier branches come off in three cuts, so the bark does not tear
Young trees trained early, while the cuts are still small
No topping. University of Minnesota Extension says to avoid it, and thinning cuts are the better way to lighten a crown

blocks.title: When to prune, and when to wait.
blocks.intro: Most trees are best pruned in late winter or early spring, before new growth starts. Oaks are the big exception, and in Michigan they have hard dates. Those cold months overlap Jake's South Florida winters, so ask early. Timing follows MSU Extension, the Michigan DNR, Michigan's Oak Wilt Coalition and Iowa State University Extension.

values: Late winter or early spring, before new growth
November to mid-March, when oak wilt risk is lowest
Late May to mid-June, after they leaf out
When it is safe, any time of year

rows.label: Wait
values: Early summer, right after new growth comes in
Do not prune April 15 through July 15
Early spring, unless you are fine with sap on the bark
On oaks from mid-March through October, paint any cut right away

rows.label: Why
values: Bare branches are easy to read, and cuts start closing in spring
Beetles carry oak wilt to fresh cuts, and infected red oaks die
Maples run a lot of sap when cut in early spring
Cleanup pruning does little or no harm in most seasons

blocks.title: If you have oaks, **read this one.**
blocks.intro: Oak wilt has been gaining ground in Michigan, and it comes with the one pruning date nobody should ignore.

items.title: How it spreads
items.body: Small sap beetles carry the oak wilt fungus to fresh cuts and wounds, and from there it moves through shared roots to nearby oaks. Once a red oak is infected it generally cannot be saved, and it often dies within a month or two.

items.title: When to leave oaks alone
items.body: The Michigan DNR and MSU Extension both say not to prune oaks from April 15 through July 15. Michigan's Oak Wilt Coalition goes further and says to leave them alone from mid-March through October. That leaves November to mid-March, when Jake is working South Florida, so ask early. He will tell you whether he can get to your oak or who can.

items.title: When a cut has to be sealed
items.body: Most trees do not need pruning paint. Iowa State University Extension says it does not stop decay and may get in the way of the tree's own response. Oaks are the exception: a cut made in the risk months gets latex paint or shellac right away, before beetles find it. A fresh oak stump counts as a wound too.

items.title: What to watch for
items.body: Red oaks that drop leaves fast in the middle of summer, some of them still green, are the warning sign, and a lab test confirms it. Do not move the firewood. If you suspect oak wilt, the Oak Wilt Coalition says to call an arborist and report it to the Michigan DNR. That is our advice too.

blocks.title: Our home town has a lot of grown-up trees.
body: HD Landscape is based in St. Clair Shores, and we trim trees and take down smaller ones here often. Much of the city was built out after the Second World War, so plenty of yards have trees that were planted small and have had decades to fill in.

The strip from the sidewalk to the curb is a different story. Trees there are public trees, maintained by the city's Forestry Division, so those stay the city's to trim. On your side of the sidewalk, a tree planted too close to the house or under the wires does not get better with age, and it is a much easier job while it is small. If yours is still a size we can handle, that is a quick conversation.

blocks.title: Good advice before the first cut.

faq.q: Do you do tree trimming in St. Clair Shores?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape does tree trimming and smaller tree removal in St. Clair Shores, our home town, and across Metro Detroit. Trees along the curb here are public trees, maintained by the city's Forestry Division, so the work we take on is on your side of the sidewalk.
Yes, for smaller trees. HD Landscape cuts them down, cleans up and can grind the stump too. Bigger ones we sub out, and the first walk will show which kind of job you have.

faq.q: How much does tree trimming cost?
faq.a: The tree sets the number: how big it is, how much needs to come off and what sits underneath it. A photo by text gets things started, and a free itemized estimate follows.

faq.q: What month is best to trim trees in Michigan?
faq.a: Late winter or early spring, just before new growth starts, is the healthiest time for most trees, according to MSU Extension. Early summer, right after new growth comes in, is the least desirable. Oaks have their own rule: do not prune them from April 15 through July 15.

faq.q: When can I prune oak trees in Michigan?
faq.a: Between November and mid-March, when the risk of oak wilt is lowest. MSU Extension and the Michigan DNR say not to prune oaks between April 15 and July 15, and Michigan's Oak Wilt Coalition says to hold off from mid-March through October. If an oak gets cut or broken in those months, paint the wound with latex paint or shellac right away. Jake will tell you whether he can get to it or who can, since he works South Florida in winter.

faq.q: How do I know if my tree is too big for you?
faq.a: Jake looks at the height, the size of the limbs and what is underneath, like a roof, a garage or wires. Smaller trees are ours, bigger ones he hands off, and you will know which yours is after the first walk.

faq.q: Do you trim trees near power lines?
faq.a: No. Iowa State University Extension says to always let the utility company handle broken limbs or tree damage around power lines, and we agree. Please do not try that one yourself either.

faq.q: Should I top my tree to make it shorter?
faq.a: We steer people away from it. University of Wisconsin Extension says trees should never be topped, because it leads to poor branch structure and more limb breakage. If a tree is too big for its spot, thinning it or taking it out is usually the better answer.

faq.q: How much of a tree can you prune at one time?
faq.a: Less than most people think. University of Wisconsin Extension caps a young tree at a third of the crown at one time, and University of Minnesota Extension caps maples and other sap-running trees at a quarter of the live foliage. A well trained older tree needs little pruning at all.

faq.q: Should I paint a pruning cut?
faq.a: Usually not. Iowa State University Extension says pruning paint does not prevent decay and may interfere with the tree's natural wound response. The exception is an oak cut during the risk months, which should get latex paint or shellac right away.

faq.q: Can you take down a tree and grind the stump too?
faq.a: Yes. We can handle both on a smaller tree. One customer had us cut down a tree and grind the stump as part of a bigger yard job, along with trimming, planting and mulch. [Stump grinding](/stump-grinding/) leaves wood shavings behind, so tell us what you want in that spot next.

faq.q: A storm broke a limb. Can you help?
faq.a: If it is a smaller tree, text Jake a photo and he will say what we can do. A big limb or a tree on a house is past what we take on, and anything near wires belongs to the utility.
